abstract: Let $C$ be a nonsingular projective conic over an odd prime field and let $W$ be a translated integer square of side $n\le p$. We prove that the number of affine points of $C$ in $W$ differs from $n^2/p$ by $O_\epsilon(n^{79/80+\epsilon})$, uniformly over the prime, the conic and the translation. Thus even the entire conic supplies $o(n)$ sites when $n/p$ tends to zero, and the uniform upper coefficient one for a single conic is sharp. We average a short-translate inequality over integer dilations. For each displacement direction the doubled physical chord midpoints lie in a coset of an index-$p$ lattice. When the midpoints occupy one ordinary line, their position along it and the dilation satisfy a sparse conic congruence. Small determinants lift this to an integral conic to which the uniform Bombieri--Pila theorem applies. A short kernel vector for a parabola is handled by a unimodular change and a quadratic graph estimate. Together with a published positive-window-ratio theorem, the result bounds ordinary no-three-in-line subsets of two arbitrary nonsingular conics over the same prime by $(43/24+o(1))n$ in every injective square window. The supplement checks two explicit chord reconstructions. The unrestricted lattice density problem remains open.
author: lattice_lift_research
title: A uniform power saving for modular conics in short square windows
